partners.mechanism_chain: ZAP70 (HGNC:12540) —DISRUPTS→ T cell receptor signaling (WP:WP467); T cell receptor signaling (WP:WP467) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); MTR (HGNC:7509) —DISRUPTS→ Methylcobalamin (CHEBI:17402); Methylcobalamin (CHEBI:17402) —DECREASES→ One-carbon metabolism and DNA synthesis (WP:WP400); One-carbon metabolism and DNA synthesis (WP:WP400) —LEADS_TO→ Megaloblastic anemia (HP:0001874); One-carbon metabolism and DNA synthesis (WP:WP400) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in ZAP70 disrupt T cell receptor signaling, leading to combined immunodeficiency. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in MTR impair cobalamin metabolism, specifically the conversion of homocysteine to methionine, which is crucial for DNA synthesis. The convergence lies in the essentiality of both ZAP70-mediated signaling for T cell function and MTR-dependent one-carbon metabolism for DNA synthesis, both of which are vital for a healthy immune system and overall development. Impaired DNA synthesis can indirectly affect rapidly dividing immune cells, and compromised T cell function can exacerbate the systemic effects of metabolic dysregulation.

partners.diseaseBName: inclusion body myopathy with Paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia type 1
partners.mechanism_chain: ZAP70 (HGNC:12790) —DISRUPTS→ T cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP402); T cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP402) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002710); VCP (HGNC:12154) —DISRUPTS→ Proteostasis (GO:0006464); Proteostasis (GO:0006464) —LEADS_TO→ Inclusion body myopathy (HP:0003697); Proteostasis (GO:0006464) —LEADS_TO→ Paget disease of bone (HP:0002729); Proteostasis (GO:0006464) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal dementia (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in ZAP70 disrupt T cell receptor signaling, leading to combined immunodeficiency. **Proposed mechanism:** ZAP70 (HGNC:12700) —DISRUPTS→ T cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP46); T cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP46) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002717); VCP (HGNC:12450) —DISRUPTS→ Proteostasis (GO:0042724); Proteostasis (GO:0042724) —LEADS_TO→ Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (HP:0003198). Loss-of-function mutations in ZAP70 disrupt T cell receptor signaling, leading to combined immunodeficiency. Gain-of-function mutations in VCP disrupt proteostasis, contributing to Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Y. The convergence is the shared pathway of proteostasis, which is critical for neuronal health and immune cell function.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of mutations in ZAP70 that cause a neuropathy phenotype or mutations in VCP that cause an immunodeficiency phenotype would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The absence of pathogenic variants in ZAP70 (for disease A) or VCP (for disease B) in large population databases like gnomAD would strengthen the claim of rarity, but not directly falsify the mechanistic link.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of VCP in proteostasis, even when mutated in different contexts, could reveal therapeutic strategies that target the broader cellular maintenance machinery. For instance, therapies aimed at improving proteostasis might offer benefits in both neurological and immunological disorders, depending on the specific VCP mutation and its downstream effects.
